angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 589,954 km at 110.35 pc = 0.07 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 9.0623 +/- 0.0101 mas (same row, RUWE 0.90): 110.35 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.848 +/- 0.011 solar radii from Nielsen et al. 2020, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-125 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020MNRAS.492.5399N/abstract): 589,954 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.859 +/- 0.044 solar masses from Nielsen et al. 2020, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-125 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020MNRAS.492.5399N/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5320 +/- 39 K from Nielsen et al. 2020, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-125 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020MNRAS.492.5399N/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Nielsen et al. 2020, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-125 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020MNRAS.492.5399N/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-125.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.515, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
